newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil CVRD sell-off seen sailing smoothly.
newsitem.headline: Brazil CVRD sell-off seen sailing smoothly.

text.p: The privatization of Brazilian state mining giant Companhia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD) is proceeding smoothly as rules for the company's sell-off brought no surprises, analysts said.
The rules for the three-phase privatization of the world's largest iron ore producer were published on Friday in the government's official gazette.
"CVRD's privatization process is running smoothly," Nomura Securities said in a report. "All the main barriers to the initial state of privatization have been overcome, or nearly so."

The government has yet to announce a minimum price and other details for the auction of an initial block of 40-45 percent of CVRD's voting shares which are expected to be sold off in mid-February on the Rio de Janeiro stock exchange.
"The auction will take place on time. I don't see any problems," said Felipe Zaghen of Banco Indosuez.
The value of the company is being estimated at $10 billion, but could increase by at least another $600 million due to the exemption of exports from the so-called ICMS tax.

Zaghen said the auction was unlikely to achieve a sale price much above the minimum price given the restrictions placed on strategic players who wanted to participate in CVRD's privatization. He estimated without these restrictions the actual sale price could well exceed the minimum price by 40-50 percent.

"The government has limited significantly the administrative and strategic action of the new owners of Vale," he said. "We do not expect a major premium for the controlling block given the limitations imposed on the participation of strategic players in the company's capital, the government's golden shares and the issue of debentures."

Under the privatization rules, steel producers of more than 8.5 million tonnes a year and iron ore producers and traders of more than 30 million tonnes annually will be limited to buying a maximum of 10 percent of the block sale.
The government will maintain two "golden shares" both in CVRD and the special purpose company (SPE) which is to be created by the buyers of the 40-45 percent share block.
The golden shares are to ensure the rules of the SPE are observed for five years and to give the government a permanent veto on changes in CVRD's iron ore, railway and ports business.
CVRD will also issue debentures linked to the company's future revenues to protect the rights of current shareholders over future mineral reserves.
Nomura said that, while the published sale terms brought no surprises, the outlook for privatization was likely to boost CVRD stock.
"We believe the privatization effect is most likely to boost CVRD's stock as the privatization in February approaches," Nomura said.

Immediately after the block sale, 5.11 percent of CVRD's capital stock will be offered to employees, followed by a global public offer of the government's remaining stake in CVRD. The government owns 76 percent of the companies voting capital, equivalent to 51 percent of CVRD's total capital.
CVRD plans to launch a Level 2 or Level 3 American Depositary Receipt along with the sale of the third block, according to Nomura.
A Sao Paulo bolsa blue chip, CVRD prefered fell 1.14 percent to end at 20.75 reais on Friday after publication of the sell-off terms. Its common ended flat at 26.00 reais.
-- Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151
